items.title: Lupin CIO Rakesh Bhardwaj on AI in Pharma Manufacturing | Front Page
items.summary:
India supplies roughly 47% of all US generic prescriptions, making pharmaceutical manufacturing one of the highest-stakes environments for AI deployment. Unlike software bugs that cost money, manufacturing or quality errors in pharma directly impact patient safety. Following the FDA and EMA’s joint release of 10 guiding principles for AI across the medicines lifecycle, drug manufacturers face a complex challenge: leveraging AI for decision advantage without compromising accountability.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Rakesh Bhardwaj, Global CIO at Lupin, to break down how pharma navigates AI adoption. They discuss the four A’s of AI (Assistant, Augmentation, Agentic, and Arterial), maintaining human-in-the-loop accountability for defect-free quality, aligning global compliance across the EU AI Act and FDA frameworks, and building supply chain control towers for end-to-end visibility.

How can pharmaceutical leaders scale AI efficiency while keeping human safety at the center?

items.title: 10 20 70. Your CFO Will Hate It.
items.summary: In episode 1019 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, @JonKrohnLearns talks with Priyanka Vergadia, better known to her quarter million strong developer community as the cloud girl, about her revolutionary 10-20-70 framework for AI budgets. She argues that 70% of AI investment should go towards employee education and upskilling, not just tools, to foster effective AI habits and achieve meaningful return on investment. Priyanka explains that AI adoption follows a J-curve, requiring sustained effort over 6-8 months before significant productivity gains appear, challenging traditional short-term spending mindsets.

items.title: Falcon 2 Beats ElevenLabs: Inside MURF AI’s Ultra-Low Latency Voice Agent | Front Page
items.summary:
MURF AI has launched Falcon 2, a lightweight, low-latency text-to-speech (TTS) model engineered specifically for conversational voice agents. Built with a primary research and engineering base in India, Falcon 2 achieves sub-100 millisecond time-to-first-byte latency while operating at roughly one-fifth the cost of comparable offerings from competitors like ElevenLabs. Rather than relying on heavy LLMs, Falcon 2 separates context and linguistic processing to optimize performance on commodity GPUs, making it ideal for code-mixed speech, localized accents, and real-time enterprise deployments.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Sneha Roy, Co-Founder & COO of MURF AI, to break down the technical breakthroughs behind Falcon 2. They discuss shifting from creative voiceovers to real-time conversational AI, solving latency and concurrency constraints for enterprise scale, navigating the unique nuances of Indian code-mixed languages, and building a lean, research-driven speech AI stack.

Can domain-focused speech models beat multi-billion-dollar frontier labs on real-time naturalness and price?
